tagline: A short road through the hardwoods to half a bridge.
intro: Route 3011 leaves US 6 near Mount Jewett and goes north through McKean County hardwood forest to Kinzua Bridge State Park, where the Kinzua Viaduct once carried the Erie's trains 301 feet above Kinzua Creek.

The first bridge went up in iron in 1882, and six of its 20 towers stood taller than the Brooklyn Bridge. Rebuilt in steel in 1900, it still held trains to five miles an hour. On July 21, 2003, a tornado brought eleven towers down in less than 30 seconds. The state left them where they fell.
season: October, when the scenic overlook in the park is a prime place to see the fall foliage.

moments.title: Mount Jewett
moments.text: A ridge-top borough at 2,240 feet, among the highest towns in Pennsylvania, named for the president of the railroad that brought the line through.

moments.title: Kinzua Sky Walk
moments.text: A walkway runs out along the standing towers to a platform partly floored in glass at the end, where the fallen towers lie below in the valley.
